text:
maria: Heads-up — we've seen client SDKs start sending a new `X-Embed-Units` header in prod. Some tenants are getting routed to slowpath despite dims matching. Need quick sync on backcompat + telemetry before we flip any console flags.

kevin: Do we know which router/condition is treating `X-Embed-Units` as authoritative? I thought routing still primarily uses the dims header and payload size.

alex: My read from the logs: if `X-Embed-Units` exists we do an extra validation step. If validation fails (malformed or > quota) we short-circuit to the conservative route. A couple SDK versions emit it as a string list instead of an int.

maria: @alex can you paste the log snippet that shows the validation error?

alex: Sure — from runtime-ingress on tenant-42:
```
2026-03-19T18:12:03Z WARN ingress: header X-Embed-Units parse error: "[64]" -> fallback to slowpath route (route=embed-safe, reason=units-parse-fail)
```

sasha: Oof. That's the JSON-y client older JS SDK. DevEx pushed a change that emits `[dim]` for multi-dim requests. We need clear contract: is `X-Embed-Units` a scalar unit estimate or list per-dim?

kevin: We previously documented only `X-Embed-Dims` and `Content-Length` as the inputs for routing. `X-Embed-Units` was an internal experiment. If SDKs leak it now, we must treat it as opt-in and not change routing semantics.

maria: Agreed. Proposal: 1) Make router tolerant — accept both scalar and array but only if parseable. 2) Emit telemetry metric `ingress.header.X-Embed-Units.present` and `ingress.route.reason` tags for two weeks. 3) Add a console breakdown per-tenant: proportion of requests hitting safe vs fast route and top header parse failures.

alex: Implemented tolerant parse as a quick patch in canary. Will return parse success tag: `embed_units.parse=ok|fail`. Also adding `ingress.route.selected` tag with values `fast|safe|fallback`.

kevin: For the console UX: surface a toggle to "honor X-Embed-Units" but default OFF. Add a tooltip: "Only enable if your client is on SDK>=v2.3 and you have consistent integer units."

sasha: For rollout: dogfood internally for 48h with toggle ON + synthetic traffic from old and new SDKs. Then 7-day opt-in for a small percentage of tenants, with telemetry gating. If parse_fail rate > 0.5% or latency delta > 5ms, auto-revert.

maria: Sounds good. Can we also add a cheap preflight in the SDK that avoids sending `X-Embed-Units` when it's ambiguous? DevEx can ship a patch.

devex-bot: New patch available: `js-sdk@2.3.1` (fix: emit scalar `X-Embed-Units` for single-dim, omit header when uncertain). Release notes: https://internal.dev.ex/patch/2.3.1

alex: I'll wire the telemetry now. Quick checklist:
- `ingress.header.X-Embed-Units.present` (bool)
- `embed_units.parse` (ok/fail)
- `ingress.route.selected` (fast/safe/fallback)
- `ingress.latency.route_selection_ms`

kevin: Console panels:
- per-tenant route split (pie)
- header parse failure rate (timeseries)
- top offending SDK versions (table)

maria: OK owners: Alex runtime + Kevin console + DevEx for SDK. Plan: patch canary today, collect telemetry for 48h, dogfood toggle next Wednesday, 1% tenant opt-in Friday. I'll write the rollout doc.

sasha: Add a runbook note: if many tenants hit slowpath, flip toggle off and enable an emergency client-side shim to remove header at ingress LB.

kevin: Also add an alert: `embed.header.parse_fail.rate > 0.5%` for 15m -> paging to eng-oncall.

maria: Great — thanks all. I'll post the rollout doc in #eng-releases and link the console mock in the ticket.
